gaps.sentence: He went on ___ even after the audience had left.
gaps.explanation: go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on to do = do something next.
deny + -ing or having + past participle: denied doing/having done. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.
gaps.explanation: 'to' is a preposition in look forward to, so -ing follows: hearing.

gaps.sentence: He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
The children are looking forward to ___ Father Christmas.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: looking forward to meeting.
hope takes the to-infinitive: hope to hear.

gaps.sentence: I've always wanted ___ how to sail.
